label: digit 0 input at original positions 2-5
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the digit 0 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at positions 2-5. It never fires on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (5 stray copy-phase activations out of 53k). Position matters: no activation at position 0, only tiny ones (~0.06 of max) at position 1, near-deterministic firing at positions 2-4 (they carry ~98% of the mass, peaking at position 3), and about half of zeros at position 5 fire, weakly (2% of mass). Nothing fires at position 6 or later. Almost all of the predicate false positives are position-5 zeros; splitting them by L did not separate them. Firing rate is higher when the sequence has more digits, which follows from the requirement for a 0. The top activations are a 0 at position 3 after three letters.

issues: The claims check out. Every activation is on input token 0. 53,442 of 53,447 dev activations are in the original phase, with 5 in the copy phase and 0 on the delimiter. Positions 0 and 6 and later have no activations. Position 1 has 552 activations, all tiny (about 0.06 of max). Positions 2 to 4 have about 98% of the activation mass, and position 3 has the most (0.439 mass at a count similar to t=2).
Position 2-4 zeros fire almost every time: (in_tok==0)&(phase==0)&(t in 2..4) scores dev precision 1.0.

The only false-positive class is position-5 zeros (dev precision 0.538, 10,963 predicted; 2% of mass). I tried to split it by digits seen before, an earlier 0, previous token digit vs letter, vowels, first token, and L. Every split stays between 0.49 and 0.62 precision. Only the identity of the previous token moves it in a graded way (prev a: 0.72, prev z: 0.33). That looks like a weak threshold effect that depends on the token, not a clean rule a predicate could capture.
The test misses on the predicate are all the tiny position-1 zeros (601 steps, 0.1% of mass). Adding t>=1 drops test F1 to 0.832, so leaving position 1 out is right.

Minor overclaim: the label says 'positions 2-5', but position 5 is only about half-reliable and weak. The explanation says this explicitly, so I accept it. Reproduced test scores: P 0.912, R 0.989, F1 0.949, mass recall 0.999.
